Heard Miss Ranjita Raddi Alagawadi, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.Girija S.Hiremath,
learned HCGP for the State.

2. The petitioner herein is accused No.1 in Crime No.267/2022 which is registered by the respondent/police for the offences punishable u/sec.498-A, 304-B, 302 r/w Section 34 of I.P.C. and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
The petitioner herein is the husband of the deceased.
Their marriage was performed by the complainant.
The said marriage is the 2nd marriage of the petitioner.
As per the averments of the complaint, the husband and wife were living happily for some time.
Thereafter, the petitioner used to assault the deceased in one or the other pretext and also harassing her both mentally and physically.
The couple had child of 1  year.
It is stated in NC: 2023:KHC-D:13372 the complaint that the petitioner herein was not taking care of the deceased properly.
On 24.12.2022 at about 11.30 a.m., the deceased called to the mobile phone of the complainant and asked him to get her currency recharged to the mobile and thereafter she stopped talking.
After some time, the complainant came to know that her daughter died in the matrimonial home by hanging herself.
A complaint came to be registered against the husband and others.
FIR registered against the petitioner herein and others.
However in the charge sheet, rest of the relatives have been left out and only the petitioner arrayed as accused.
4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence.
Initially a complaint was lodged against all the family members of the accused.
However, during investigation, they found the allegations made against the petitioner only.
It is further submitted that there is no nexus between the abatement and suicide.
There is one more complaint regarding ill-treatment, harassment and cruelty prior to the date of incident.
Except omnibus allegations made against all the accused in the complaint, no overt- act attributed against the petitioner herein.

The alleged offence is neither punishable with death nor imprisonment for Basavaraj Hosalli vs The State Of Karnataka on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47247588/
2 life.

sentences.text: The offence which is punishable u/sec.306 of IPC is punishable with imprisonment for 10 years.

The petitioner is the earning member of the family and he has to take care of the child who is aged about 1  year and he is the permanent resident of Belahud village and he will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submits that the alleged offence is heinous in nature.
The incident had taken place in the house of the petitioner.
The NC: 2023:KHC-D:13372 harassment, cruelty and ill-treatment has been narrated in the complaint by the complainant who is the mother of the deceased.
There are witnesses to the ill-treatment and harassment.
If the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there may be chances of absconding and also threatening the prosecution witnesses.
Making such submission, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the averments of the charge sheet.
8.
Admittedly, the petitioner is the husband of the deceased and it is the 2nd marriage for the petitioner.
The couple had child of 1  year.
Both were living happily for some time.
After some time, there were difference of opinion between them.
As per the averments of the charge sheet, the petitioner used to harass the deceased in one or the other pretext and she was being harassed by the petitioner and his family members.
Initially a complaint was lodged against the petitioner and his family members.
In the charge sheet after investigation, the name of the petitioner continued as accused.
However rest of the family members have been left out.
The alleged offence is punishable with imprisonment for 10 years.
After reading the charge sheet material in respect of abatement to commit suicide, without adverting to the merits of the case, it is appropriate to grant bail.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also responsibility of the petitioner, it is appropriate to grant bail by imposing suitable conditions.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner/accused No.1 is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.267/2022 of Gadag Rural Police Station for the offence punishable u/sec.498-A, 304-B, 302 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, subject to the following:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13372 CONDITIONS a) The petitioner shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one surety for the likesum.

3 b) The petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing.
Sd/-
